source_text: Hinc haereses et factae sunt frequenter et fiunt, dum perversa mens non habet pacem, dum perfidia discordans non tenet unitatem. Fieri vero haec Dominus permittit et patitur, manente propriae libertatis arbitrio, ut, dum corda nostra et mentes nostras veritatis discrimen examinat, probatorum fides integra manifesta luce clarescat. Per Apostolum praemonet Spiritus sanctus et dicit: Oportet haereses esse, ut probati manifesti sint in vobis. Sic probantur fideles, sic perfidi deteguntur. Sic et ante judicii diem hic quoque jam justorum atque injustorum animae dividuntur, et a frumento paleae separantur. Hi sunt qui se ultro apud temerarios convenas sine divina dispositione praeficiunt, qui, se praepositos sine ulla ordinationis lege constituunt, qui, nemine episcopatum dante, episcopi sibi nomen assumunt; quos designat in Psalmis Spiritus sanctus sedentes in pestilentiae cathedra, pestes et lues fidei, serpentis ore fallentes, et corrumpendae veritatis artifices, venena lethalia linguis pestiferis evomentes; quorum sermo ut cancer serpit, quorum tractatus pectoribus et cordibus singulorum mortale virus infundit.
pass_a_gloss: From this, heresies have been made frequently and are being made, while the perverse mind does not have peace, while perfidious discord does not hold unity. But the Lord permits and suffers these things to happen, with the judgment of His own liberty remaining, so that, while He examines the discernment of truth in our hearts and minds, the intact faith of those who have been tested may shine with manifest light. Through the Apostle, the Holy Spirit forewarns and says: It is necessary that there be heresies, so that those who have been tested may be manifest among you. Thus the faithful are tested, thus the perfidious are uncovered. Thus also, before the day of judgment, the souls of the just and the unjust are already divided here, and the chaff is separated from the wheat. These are the ones who voluntarily gather among the rash without divine disposition, who constitute themselves as prelates without any law of ordination, who, with no one giving them the episcopate, assume the name of bishop for themselves; whom the Holy Spirit designates in the Psalms as sitting in the chair of pestilence, pests and plagues of the faith, deceiving with the serpent's mouth, and artisans of corrupting the truth, vomiting lethal poisons with pestilential tongues; whose speech creeps like a cancer, whose dealings pour mortal poison into the breasts and hearts of individuals.

choices.english: It is necessary that there be heresies
those who have been tested may be manifest

pass_b_english: From this, heresies have often arisen and still arise, while a perverse mind lacks peace and faithless discord fails to keep unity. Yet the Lord allows and endures these things, since the freedom of His own will remains, so that while He examines the discernment of truth in our hearts and minds, the unshaken faith of the tested may shine in clear light. Through the Apostle the Holy Spirit forewarns and says: "There must be heresies, so that those who are approved may be revealed among you" (1 Corinthians 11:19). Thus the faithful are proved, thus the faithless are exposed. Thus even now, before the day of judgment, the souls of the just and the unjust are already divided here, and the chaff is separated from the wheat. These are the ones who push themselves forward among the reckless without divine appointment, who set themselves up as prelates without any law of ordination, who take the title of bishop for themselves though no one has given them the episcopate. The Holy Spirit marks them in the Psalms as sitting in the chair of pestilence, as pests and plagues of the faith, deceiving with a serpent's mouth and crafting the corruption of truth, vomiting lethal poisons with pestilential tongues; their speech creeps like cancer, and their dealings pour mortal poison into the breasts and hearts of individuals.

Pass B correctly identifies and adds the scripture citation (1 Corinthians 11:19) for the quoted phrase 'Oportet haereses esse, ut probati manifesti sint in vobis', which is required by the rules for scripture identification. Pass A and B are consistent with the Latin source.
